candidates.exact_span: The following Minimum Quantification Levels (MQL's) are to be used for reporting pollutant data for NPDES permit applications and/or compliance reporting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether MQLs govern compliance reporting (not just permit applications) determines if sub-MQL or non-quantified results must be handled under these thresholds for limit comparisons (A), whether compliance reporting itself is within scope of these quantification rules (B), and how missing or below-MQL results are classified versus ordinary numeric results (C).

candidates.exact_span: NPDES permit applications and/or compliance reporting
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 'and/or' scope is ambiguous: if MQL rules apply only to applications, compliance-period monitoring obligations and missing-evidence handling for reported data may differ from if they also bind compliance reporting.

Two distinct MQL values are listed for mercury while footnote *1 is not included in this segment; choosing 0.0005 versus 0.005 changes whether mercury results are treated as quantified, how they are compared to any applicable limit (A), and whether mercury monitoring periods are classified as having an ordinary numeric result or a below-MQL/no-data state (C).

MQLs are specified in micrograms per liter; if reported measurements or permit limits use different units or conversion assumptions, the applicable MQL threshold and whether a measurement exceeds the limit can change.
